blocks.h2: Signs Your Elgin Water Heater Needs Repair
blocks.intro: These are the calls we take most:

tiles.body: A gas burner that won't stay lit or an electric element that's failed leaves you with half a tank of hot water.
Brown water from the hot side only often means the tank is corroding or the anode rod is used up.
Sediment on the tank bottom traps water that boils under it. A flush may help if it's caught early.

tiles.h3: A Wet Floor by the Tank
tiles.body: A valve or fitting drip is a repair. A leak from the tank body means it's done.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Problems in Elgin Homes
blocks.intro: Elgin's homes span more than 150 years, so the water heater setup in your basement depends a lot on when the house was built.

items.body: In homes near downtown, gas water heaters often vent into an old masonry chimney. If the furnace was upgraded and now vents through the wall, the heater may be left venting alone into a flue that's too big. We check the draft on every gas heater.

items.h3: Original Heaters on the West Side
items.body: Nearly 3 in 10 Elgin homes went up between 1990 and 2009. A heater that came with the house is long past its expected life. If yours is original, it's worth a look before it fails.
Elgin treats Fox River water. Treated water still carries some minerals, and they settle in the bottom of the tank over time. Yearly flushing keeps that layer thin.

bodies: We service every type of residential water heater you'll find in Elgin: gas and electric tanks, power-vent models, high-efficiency condensing units and tankless heaters. We diagnose first and recommend second.

Look at the label on the side of your tank. It shows the fuel, the size and the manufacture date, usually inside the serial number. Read it to us when you call and we'll know a lot before we arrive. If it's time for a new one, see [water heater installation](/elgin/water-heater-installation).
A yearly flush clears the sediment that collects at the bottom of the tank. Less sediment means quieter heating, better efficiency and a longer life for the tank.

A maintenance visit includes the flush, a test of the temperature and pressure relief valve, a look at the anode rod and a check of the burner or elements and the venting. Tankless units get descaled. If your heater has never been flushed, it's the place to start.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: Why is my hot water rusty but my cold water is clear?
items.preview: The tank is corroding or the anode rod is gone.
items.answer: If only the hot side is rusty, the problem is in the water heater. The anode rod, which protects the tank, may be used up, or the tank is starting to rust inside. Replacing the anode can help if the tank isn't leaking yet.

items.q: Is it worth repairing an older water heater?
items.preview: Under about 8 years, usually. Over 12, usually not.
items.answer: If the heater is under about 8 years old and a part failed, repair usually makes sense. Past 12 years, or if the tank leaks, replacement is the better value. Between those, we'll lay out both.

items.q: How long do water heaters last in Elgin?
items.preview: Tank heaters usually last about 8 to 12 years.
items.answer: Tank water heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years. Regular flushing helps them reach the longer end.

items.q: What should I do if my water heater is leaking?
items.preview: Shut off the cold water to the tank and call.
items.answer: Turn off the cold water valve on top of the tank. On a gas heater, set the control to pilot or off. Put a bucket or towels down and call us. If you smell gas, leave and call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside.

items.q: How much does water heater repair cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on the part and the heater. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what failed, the type of heater and the parts. We diagnose it and give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
